question: Will ECDC report locally acquired human West Nile virus cases in 17 or more countries in its 2026 weekly surveillance update published around 18 September 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 15 countries at the 3 Sep 2026 cut-off; YES needs +2 in 13 days (at most two weekly updates). Reference class — ECDC WNV seasons already at 15+ countries by early September — shows sharp deceleration: 2024 was at 16 on 3 Sep and added only 3 more over the following three months; 2025 added 4 between 3 Sep and 3 Oct from a much shallower base of 9. Naive momentum from 2026's own August pace (~1.5 new countries/week) argues YES, but that pace was driven by common reporters entering; the 15 already listed include essentially every regular except Bulgaria. Modelling the remaining pool country-by-country (Bulgaria ~0.6 given confirmed national cases and hospitalisations awaiting EpiPulse entry, Turkiye ~0.18 given chronic late reporting, Slovakia/Slovenia/Czechia/Portugal/Poland/Belgium/BiH each 0.04-0.10) gives P(>=2 additions in two updates) ~0.34-0.38. Discounting for the real possibility that the governing report is the 11 Sep publication (one update, ~0.15-0.17) because the resolution timestamp precedes the 18 Sep publication, the blend lands near 0.28. No prediction market prices this contract.

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 15 countries (data to 3 Sep 2026); YES needs +2 by the resolving cut-off, which is ~17 Sep if the 18 Sep publication counts, or ~10 Sep under a strict 18 Sep 00:00 UTC read (I weight ~75/25). Momentum looks favourable in the aggregate (6 on 22 Jul, 7 on 5 Aug, 12 on ~19 Aug, 15 on 3 Sep, i.e. ~1.5 countries/week), but that growth consumed the ripe pool: the 15 already include every 2024-list country except Bulgaria, Turkiye, Slovakia, Slovenia and Czechia, plus Netherlands. Bottom-up, only Bulgaria has a known 2026 locally acquired human case not yet in ECDC (Plovdiv, confirmed week of 17-23 Aug) and it has already shown a >2-week EpiPulse lag; the ECDC/EFSA monthly to 5 Aug records no equid/bird outbreaks at all in Bulgaria, Slovakia, Slovenia, Czechia, Portugal or Poland, so there is no animal early-warning for a second entrant. Enumerating candidate-by-candidate gives ~0.42 for the 17 Sep report and ~0.20 for the 10 Sep report; a pure trend extrapolation would give ~0.55-0.65, and I weight the structural view more because the remaining pool is thin and country-specific. Counter-case: 2024 (the record 19-country year) had Slovakia, Slovenia, Czechia, Bulgaria and Turkiye all in by the 25 Sep cut-off, so a two-country September jump is far from unprecedented, and 2026 is already broader than 2025 at the same point.

(1) Which report governs — classified factual/contract-reading and settled toward two remaining updates (~0.88 weight) on the criteria's own 'most recent weekly update published on or before 18 September' fallback plus the prompt's instruction that the criteria text alone defines the window; this raises my number relative to Runs 1 and 2, which discounted for the 18 Sep 00:00Z timestamp. What broke the tie on the final number was that the 2024 conditional analogue (16 -> 18 over 22 days, P(>=2) ~0.33) and a bottom-up Poisson-binomial over the named candidate pool (~0.32) converge independently, so I do not adopt Run 3's higher 0.42 despite agreeing with its schedule reading. Net: 0.88 x 0.33 + 0.12 x 0.15 ~= 0.31, rounded to 0.32.
